newsitem.title: FRANCE: Nine die at rebel roadblock in Algeria - paper.
newsitem.headline: Nine die at rebel roadblock in Algeria - paper.

text.p: Suspected Moslem rebels killed a family of seven and two motorists in Diblinou area near the town of Mascara in Algeria at the weekend, an Algerian newspaper said on Monday.
The main Arabic-language paper Al Khabar said an armed group erected a fake security force roadblock and intercepted the family, killing them all.
The drivers of two other cars were also caught at the roadblock, around 325 km (200 miles) southwest of Algiers, and killed.
All but two of the nine had their throats cut. The other two were shot, said the newspaper, which gave no further details.

Le Matin newspaper said a bomb wounded three people at 6 a.m. in the western city of Oran on Sunday. Another newspaper, La Tribune, said the blast in Rue Abed Mohamed near Theveny Square caused heavy damage.

Al Khabar said security forces killed two "terrorists" at the weekend. One was killed in Blida, the provincial capital some 50 km (30 miles) south of Algiers, and the other in Khemis el-Khechna, in Blida province.

Algerian officials and media use the term "terrorist" for Moslem fundamentalists who have been carrying out an armed insurgency since the authorities in January 1992 cancelled a general election dominated by the Islamic Salvation Front (FIS). The FIS is now banned.
About 60,000 people have been killed in the nearly six years of conflict.
